newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says PLMO to give tax waivers.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says PLMO to give tax waivers.

text.p: Users of Thailand's real estate rescue fund run by the Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) are likely to be eligible for a series of tax concessions, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday.
Concessions under consideration include a reduction in property transfer fees to 0.01 percent from one to two percent, and waivers on value added tax and withholding tax, the executive said.
Losses occurring from property write-downs may also be made tax deductible, the official told Reuters.
PLMO is a state agency established earlier this year to manage a 100 billion baht bond-funded bail-out programme for troubled property projects.
Developers and financial institutions are eligible to apply to the PLMO to help refinance troubled property projects.
Growing problems of commercial lenders exposed to the property sector have raised concerns of financial liquidity in the two sectors.

"The land act doesn't allow anyone to waive property transfer fees, but it will be reduced either on the transfer of mortgage or the transfer of property down from two percent and one percent top 0.01 percent," he said.

"Also we are going to ask the revenue department to waive the VAT (value added tax) and any other tax...because the cabinet issued in March recommendation that PLMO's activities should be tax free," he said.
Tax regulation changes should be made by the end of next week and the agency is expected to start its first project purchase by end-May, the official said.
Developers' eligibility for the scheme will depend on assessment of project viability and preparedness of developers to take losses by cutting prices or adjusting marketing strategies, he said.
"The PLMO will continue to consider the purchase of every type of property asset except land banks," he added.

"The general criteria also includes that financial institutions who wish to sell (property) loans to the PLMO must guarantee at least 50 percent of the loans and have to send people to report to the PLMO regularly," he said.
